strongest_angle: MIT engineers designed and built a 3-meter concrete test beam using a sewn fabric mold, achieving a massive reduction in concrete and steel usage while maintaining structural integrity.

key_facts.fact: MIT engineers built a 3-meter concrete test beam using a sewn cotton mold that required one-third the amount of concrete and half as much steel as a conventional beam.
Researchers published their findings regarding fabric-formed concrete beams in the Journal of Building Engineering, detailing automated pattern generation for topology optimization.
Load testing of the 3-meter beam showed deflection within about 2 percent of the computer model created by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology research team.
